pm_exper_user_2115_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.all_options:
(a) Ah, my friend, if you’re looking for smoother coffee, try a light to medium roast made from low-acid beans. Brewing with a French press or pour-over can bring out a gentle flavor that’s easy to enjoy at any time of day.
(b) Ah, mi amigo, since your stomach sometimes protests after darker brews, you might try a smooth medium roast made with low-acid beans—perhaps from regions like Brazil or Sumatra. Cold brew or a café de olla made with less coffee and more cinnamon can be gentle on you while still offering warmth and character.
(c) Ah, mi amigo, since darker roasts can sometimes trigger your acid reflux, you might look for a mellow medium roast or low-acid Mexican coffee from Veracruz. Brew it slowly and sip it alongside a fresh tortilla in the morning, letting the flavors settle warmly without trouble.
(d) Given that stronger coffee can sometimes stir your acid reflux, you might enjoy switching to a lighter roast with naturally low acidity, like beans from Guatemala’s Antigua region. Brewing them with a pour-over method can bring out softness in flavor without straining your comfort.
